_comment: Fragment 86 — D-130: two blocked-on-input items sized to what they actually need, one of them missing its ask entirely until now. Merged 2026-08-25.

nodes.label: An Ask Sized to the Question It Actually Is, Not to Its Neighbor's Precedent
nodes.description: A newly opened business-facing condition was given a three-question shape instead of copying the multi-section policy-framework shape of the topically adjacent condition it followed, because the question itself was narrower than the precedent it sat beside.
nodes.rationale: Matching a new item's shape to its nearest precedent rather than to what it actually requires produces asks that are either bloated or under-specified. Checking which one before drafting is what let a one-question gap stay a one-question ask instead of inheriting a five-value framework it did not need.

nodes.label: A Channel That Only Runs One Direction Was Nearly Used the Wrong Way
nodes.description: The first plan for surfacing a business-facing ask used the same directional channel a build lane uses to reach the orchestration lane, before noticing the orchestration lane cannot raise entries on that channel for itself and redirecting to the register's own condition mechanism instead.
nodes.rationale: The handoff channel's one-directional design is already established elsewhere in this corpus; the near-miss here is a reminder that a structural rule has to be re-checked at the point of use, not merely known in the abstract, and that the register itself is the correct surface for a Lane A-originated ask.
